messages.content: Help me signal the end of an XML element with the qualified name `{namespaceURI='http://www.example.com', localPart='item', prefix='ex'}` and augmentation information `augmentations` in an XML processing application that uses namespaces?

function.name: XMLNamespaceBinder_endElement
function.description: Signals the end of an XML element, handling namespace-related processing if namespaces are enabled, or delegating to the document handler otherwise. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

element.description: The qualified name of the element that is ending. Use QName object, has a constructor that takes in three parameters, namespaceURI, localPart, prefix This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

augs.description: Augmentation information associated with the element. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the tool "XMLNamespaceBinder_endElement" from the namespace functions. Provide arguments as JSON.

The element argument should represent a QName object constructed with (namespaceURI, localPart, prefix). We have namespaceURI="http://www.example.com", localPart="item", prefix="ex". So we pass something like `"QName('http://www.example.com','item','ex')"` maybe? But spec says it can be any type of Java object in string representation. So likely just provide the string representation of the QName instance. For example:

```
{
    "element": "new javax.xml.namespace.QName(\"http://www.example.com\", \"item\", \"ex\")",
    "augs": "augmentations"
}
```

But they said use QName object, has a constructor that takes in three params. So we might supply exactly that string. Let's do:

```json
{
   "element":"javax.xml.namespace.QName('http://www.example.com','item','ex')",
   "augs":"augmentations"
}
```

Better to match typical Java code: new QName("...", "...","..."). We'll produce:

```
{ 
  "element":"new javax.xml.namespace.QName(\"http://www.example.com\",\"item\",\"ex\")",
  "augs":"augmentations"
}
```

Let's output this via the tool invocation.
